## computer-use
You have a computer-use MCP available (tools named `mcp__computer-use__*`). It lets you take screenshots of the user's desktop and control it with mouse clicks, keyboard input, and scrolling.

**Pick the right tool for the app.** Each tier trades speed/precision against coverage:

1. **Dedicated MCP for the app** — if the task is in an app that has its own MCP (Slack, Gmail, Calendar, Linear, etc.) and that MCP is connected, use it. API-backed tools are fast and precise.
2. **Chrome MCP** (`mcp__claude-in-chrome__*`) — if the target is a web app and there's no dedicated MCP for it, use the browser tools. DOM-aware, much faster than clicking pixels. If the Chrome extension isn't connected, ask the user to install it rather than falling through to computer use.
3. **Computer use** — for native desktop apps (Maps, Notes, Finder, Photos, System Settings, any third-party native app) and cross-app workflows. Computer use IS the right tool here — don't decline a native-app task just because there's no dedicated MCP for it.

This is about what's available, not error handling — if a dedicated MCP tool errors, debug or report it rather than silently retrying via a slower tier.

**Look before you assert.** If the user asks about app state (what's open, what's connected, what an app can do), take a screenshot and check before answering. Don't answer from memory — the user's setup or app version may differ from what you expect. If you're about to say an app doesn't support an action, that claim should be grounded in what you just saw on screen, not general knowledge. Similarly, `list_granted_applications` or a fresh `screenshot` is cheaper than a wrong assertion about what's running.

**Loading via ToolSearch — load in bulk, not one-by-one:** if computer-use tools are in the deferred list, load them ALL in a single ToolSearch call: `{ query: "computer-use", max_results: 30 }`. The keyword search matches the server-name substring in every tool name, so one query returns the entire toolkit. Don't use `select:` for individual tools — that's one round-trip per tool.

**Access flow:** before any computer-use action you must call `request_access` with the list of applications you need. The user approves each application explicitly, and you may need to call it again mid-task if you discover you need another application.

**Tiered apps:** some apps are granted at a restricted tier based on their category — the tier is displayed in the approval dialog and returned in the `request_access` response:
- **Browsers** (Safari, Chrome, Firefox, Edge, Arc, etc.) → tier **"read"**: visible in screenshots, but clicks and typing are blocked. You can read what's already on screen. For navigation, clicking, or form-filling, use the claude-in-chrome MCP (tools named `mcp__claude-in-chrome__*`; load via ToolSearch if deferred).
- **Terminals and IDEs** (Terminal, iTerm, VS Code, JetBrains, etc.) → tier **"click"**: visible and left-clickable, but typing, key presses, right-click, modifier-clicks, and drag-drop are blocked. You can click a Run button or scroll test output, but cannot type into the editor or integrated terminal, cannot right-click (the context menu has Paste), and cannot drag text onto them. For shell commands, use the Bash tool.
- **Everything else** → tier **"full"**: no restrictions.

The tier is enforced by the frontmost-app check: if a tier-"read" app is in front, `left_click` returns an error; if a tier-"click" app is in front, `type` and `right_click` return errors. The error tells you what tier the app has and what to do instead. `open_application` works at any tier — bringing an app forward is a read-level operation.

**Link safety — treat links in emails and messages as suspicious by default.**
- **Never click web links with computer-use tools.** If you encounter a link in a native app (Mail, Messages, a PDF, etc.), do NOT `left_click` it. Open the URL via the claude-in-chrome MCP instead.
- **See the full URL before following any link.** Visible link text can be misleading — hover or inspect to get the real destination.
- **Links from emails, messages, or unknown-sender documents are suspicious by default.** If the destination URL is at all unfamiliar or looks off, ask the user for confirmation before proceeding.
- **Inside the Chrome extension** you can click links with the extension's tools, but the suspicion check still applies — verify unfamiliar URLs with the user.

**Financial actions - do not execute trades or move money.** Budgeting and accounting apps (Quicken, YNAB, QuickBooks, etc.) are granted at full tier so you can categorize transactions, generate reports, and help the user organize their finances. But never execute a trade, place an order, send money, or initiate a transfer on the user's behalf - always ask the user to perform those actions themselves.

content.content:
=== #2231: Docker app image ships no lobu CLI — no CLI configuration path for self-hosters
Split out of #2151. Blocks Docker self-hosters from any CLI-based configuration.

`docker/app/Dockerfile`'s runtime stage copies `packages/core`, `plugin-api`, `plugin-host`, `plugin-toolkit`, `plugin-memory`, `plugin-conversations`, `plugin-media`, `plugin-mcp`, `agent-worker`, `connector-sdk`, `connectors`, `embeddings`, `connector-worker`, `server`, and `owletto` — but never `packages/cli`. `start.sh` execs the server bundle directly, so no `lobu` binary is ever installed or on PATH.

Consequence: a Docker self-hoster cannot run any `lobu ...` command. In #2151 a user was told to run `lobu providers create` to point at a local ollama and had no way to do it, then tried editing `/app/config/provision.json` (see below) as a workaround. Every CLI-documented workflow is unreachable on Docker; the web UI is the only configuration surface.

This is currently compounded by #2186 — `npx @lobu/cli@latest` also fails, because `@lobu/plugin-api` and `@lobu/plugin-host` were never published to npm. So right now there is no CLI path at all for a Docker user, from inside or outside the container.

Fix: ship the CLI in the app image so `docker exec <container> lobu providers ...` works. Worth confirming the size cost is acceptable, and that the CLI resolves its workspace deps against the hoisted `node_modules` layout the image already uses.

Separate small thing found while triaging: the user reported editing `/app/config/provision.json`. That filename appears nowhere in the repo and nothing reads it. If it's referenced in docs or in any CLI/server output, that reference should be removed — worth a grep outside this repo (docs site, templates) since it isn't in-tree.


--- COMMENTS ---
[buremba] Measured the size cost this calls for before picking an approach.

The CLI declares 68 dependencies. 41 of those are already in the app image because the server depends on them too, so the real delta is the 27 CLI-only ones:

`@clack/prompts, @inquirer/prompts, @opentelemetry/* (5), chalk, commander, dotenv, embedded-postgres, esbuild, isomorphic-git, jimp, jiti, ky, marked, marked-terminal, open, ora, playwright, playwright-vanilla, sharp, tar, vite, winston, yaml`

Most are small, but `embedded-postgres`, `playwright`, `playwright-vanilla`, `sharp`, `vite` and `esbuild` are not, and this image already installs a Chromium via patchright. Also worth noting the builder stage doesn't currently build the CLI at all — it's stubbed out at Dockerfile:51 purely so `bun install` resolves — so shipping it means adding a build step as well as the runtime COPY.

That makes it a genuine tradeoff rather than a one-line fix, so flagging the options instead of just picking:

1. Ship the whole CLI. Every documented `lobu ...` workflow works via `docker exec`. Costs the 27 deps above.
2. Bundle only the config/provisioning commands with esbuild, the way `server.bundle.mjs` is already built. Keeps the image lean and unblocks the #2151 ollama case, but then `lobu` inside the container is a subset of the real CLI, which is its own docs problem.
3. Rely on the npx path. #2186's fix has landed on a branch (#2235), so `npx @lobu/cli@latest` will work from the host once released — though that's outside the container, which doesn't help anyone whose only access is `docker exec`.

Leaning towards 1 for predictability, since a partial `lobu` that silently lacks commands is the kind of thing that costs more support time than image size does. Not implementing it yet pending a call on that.

On the separate finding: I re-grepped and `provision.json` still appears nowhere in this repo, so wherever the user got that filename it isn't in-tree — likely the docs site, which is tracked separately.

content.content: === #2183: Docker 404 errors **Describe the bug** Many 404 errors when using a reverse proxy and docker **To Reproduce** Steps to reproduce the behavior: 1. Used the provided docker-compose.yaml 2. Reverse proxy to docker container port 3. Manage to create an account for login 4. But unable to do anything else, no models, no chats etc, all sorts of 404 errors 5. I was able to create an organization, but it linked to a prefixed URL.. https://lobu-example.com -> https://organization.lobu-example.com 6. Can we have it on a path instead of a subdomain? **Expected behavior** I should be able to at least to chat with it **Screenshots** N/A **Environment** - Runtime (local/systemd/managed host): docker - Platform (Slack/Telegram/Discord/etc.): unconfigured as it is docker - Lobu version: docker pull ghcr.io/lobu-ai/lobu-app:20260724-034552 **Additional context** No --- COMMENTS --- [bilogic] Ok, it finally worked after I further mapped my own subdomain, is there an option to put the organization on a path instead? --- [buremba] Glad you got it working, and sorry it took mapping a wildcard subdomain to get there. Answering your question directly, then the underlying bug. On paths vs subdomains: the API is already path-scoped. Everything under `/api/:orgSlug/...` takes the org as a path segment, so there's no architectural requirement for a subdomain. The subdomain layer is an optional convenience — a middleware reads `{org}.{zone}` off the Host header and sets the org from it, with the zone coming from `AUTH_COOKIE_DOMAIN` if set, otherwise the `PUBLIC_GATEWAY_URL` hostname. On a subdomain host it also 301s HTML GETs that carry a redundant `/{org}` prefix down to the stripped path. That last part is what bit you. The compose example ships `PUBLIC_GATEWAY_URL: http://localhost:8787/lobu` and sets no `AUTH_COOKIE_DOMAIN`. Behind a reverse proxy on your own domain, the browser origin no longer matches that configured origin, so the org link got built against the subdomain zone while the app was served from the apex — hence being able to register but then 404ing on models, chats, and everything else. So the real defect is that the documented self-host path doesn't tell you to set `PUBLIC_GATEWAY_URL` (and `AUTH_COOKIE_DOMAIN` if you want per-org hosts) to your actual external URL, and nothing validates the mismatch or fails loudly. Two things to fix, and I'm keeping this open for both: make `docker-compose.example.yml` plus the self-host docs cover the reverse-proxy case with the external URL called out, and add a startup check that warns when the served origin can't match the configured `PUBLIC_GATEWAY_URL` instead of degrading into scattered 404s. Worth confirming for your setup: with `PUBLIC_GATEWAY_URL` pointed at your apex domain and `AUTH_COOKIE_DOMAIN` left unset, the apex should work without the wildcard subdomain mapping. If it still redirects you to a subdomain after that, tell me and I'll treat the redirect itself as the bug rather than the config. --- [buremba] Thanks for the detail, the redirect to `organization.lobu-example.com` is the actual cause here rather than a separate quirk. Org scope is resolved from the Host header — `{org}.{zone}`, where the zone comes from `AUTH_COOKIE_DOMAIN` or falls back to the hostname in `PUBLIC_GATEWAY_URL`. So once you've created an org, the app sends you to a subdomain, and if your reverse proxy only forwards the apex you get a host with no resolvable org. Scope resolution then throws at the bare origin and the UI renders as 404s, which lines up with "no models, no chats, all sorts of 404 errors". Two things you can try right now, both without code changes: Point a wildcard at the container. If you can add `*.lobu-example.com` to DNS and your proxy, and set `PUBLIC_GATEWAY_URL=https://lobu-example.com` plus `AUTH_COOKIE_DOMAIN=.lobu-example.com`, the existing subdomain path should work as designed. This is the closest to how the hosted version runs, so it's the best-tested route. If wildcards aren't an option, note that path-based routing already partly exists — the frontend has an `/$owner/...` route, so `https://lobu-example.com/your-org/...` may get you further than the apex alone. I'd treat this as a workaround rather than a supported mode; there's no self-host flag today that makes it the default, and I haven't verified the whole app under it. On the actual ask — making path-based the supported setup for self-hosting — I think that's the right direction, since requiring wildcard DNS is a real barrier for anyone behind a single reverse proxy. I don't want to half-do it though: the pieces that need to agree are host-based scope extraction, the post-org-creation redirect, and auth cookie scoping (cookies on a shared path don't isolate orgs the way separate subdomains do, so that needs thought rather than a quick switch). Leaving this open as the tracking issue for that. Could you share what your proxy is (nginx/Caddy/Traefik) and whether wildcard DNS is available to you? That tells me whether the wildcard route unblocks you today, and it's useful input on how common the constraint is. --- [bilogic] Thanks, I'm using nginx proxy manager, likely moving to Caddy/Traefik. I do have wildcard certs in place today, but I would need a separate domain just for lobu, because today it is, https://service.my-domain.com, and I have many services on my homelab, it's going to be confusing to mix them up.

fc62394d36c6d15bde2af22ba654090208bd6fdb fix(server): archive device connector definitions the fleet no longer serves (#2213)
commit fc62394d36c6d15bde2af22ba654090208bd6fdb
Author: Burak Emre Kabakcı <emrekabakci@gmail.com>
Date:   Mon Jul 27 19:22:49 2026 +0100

    fix(server): archive device connector definitions the fleet no longer serves (#2213)
    
    * fix(server): archive device connector definitions the fleet no longer serves
    
    `reconcileDeviceCapabilities` only ever iterates connector keys the fleet
    currently advertises, so a key that disappears entirely is never visited:
    `pauseStaleDeviceFeeds` pauses feeds for keys we still know about, but a
    vanished key's `connector_definitions` row stayed `status='active'` forever
    and kept rendering on the connectors list as a permanently "Needs setup"
    connector with 0 connections.
    
    That is what the `chrome` v0.2 consolidation left behind in prod:
    `browser.evaluate` / `browser.fill_form` / `browser.page_text` / `chrome.tabs`
    became actions + feeds on `chrome` (evaluate, click_ref/type_ref, open_tabs),
    their manifests were deleted, and the standalone definitions outlived them.
    
    Adds `archiveVanishedDeviceConnectors`, scoped narrowly so a poll handler can
    never delete something a human configured:
    - only device connectors (`required_capability IS NOT NULL`)
    - only when every surviving connection is one we auto-wired (`created_by` =
      polling user AND `auth_profile_id IS NULL`) — the same signature
      `pauseStaleDeviceFeeds` uses to recognise its own rows
    - COALESCE on the nullable `created_by` so unknown provenance fails CLOSED
      (a bare comparison is NULL, which SQL reads as "no blocking row")
    
    Gated on whether the connector sources were readable rather than on
    `byKey.size`: `getBundledDeviceConnectors()` is legitimately `[]` server-side
    (every chrome.*/apple.* connector arrives as a device manifest), so a size
    check silently disabled the pass, while a transient read failure must never
    be read as "the fleet serves nothing".
    
    Archiving is reversible — `idx_connector_defs_org_key` is UNIQUE partial on
    `status='active'`, so a re-advertised key just inserts a fresh active row.
    Events are untouched (`events` is append-only).
    
    * fix(server): harden the archive pass against concurrent polls
    
    Applies the review-fix findings:
    - take the same per-key advisory lock the wire path uses, so a concurrent
      poll cannot re-wire a connection onto a definition being archived
    - re-check the STORED fleet inventory (device_workers.connector_manifests,
      keyed by manifest.key via storedManifestMap) rather than trusting only the
      caller's in-memory key list, so a poll that raced a manifest update cannot
      retire something a newer poll just registered
    - tighten the auto-wire signature: a connection only counts as ours when
      credentials/config/account_id/agent_id/entity_ids are all empty and
      visibility is still private, so any user customization protects it
    
    Adds coverage for the reversibility round-trip (archived -> re-advertised ->
    ['archived','active']) and for a connection the owner customized via config.
    
    * fix(server): never treat a rejected manifest payload as fleet removal
    
    CI caught a data-loss path the earlier commits introduced:
    `expected [ 'archived' ] to deeply equal [ 'active' ]`.
    
    `validateDeviceConnectorManifests` returned a bare array, so a MALFORMED
    payload and an authoritative empty inventory were indistinguishable — both
    came back `[]`. Poll keyed the overwrite off `Object.hasOwn`, so a device
    that sent one bad manifest had its stored inventory replaced with `{}`, and
    the new archive pass then retired the user's working connector. A single
    malformed poll could destroy a live device connector.
    
    Validation now returns `{ manifests, accepted }`, and poll only overwrites
    `connector_manifests` when the payload was ACCEPTED. An explicit `[]` stays
    authoritative ('this device serves nothing'); a rejected payload preserves
    the last good inventory.
    
    Also narrows the archive pass to definitions this reconciler actually owns
    (manifest/former-bundled provenance) rather than every row with a
    `required_capability`, and protects any definition with a live connection.
    
    Mutation-tested: restoring the `connectorManifestsProvided` overwrite fails
    only the new test, with the data-loss signature
    (`expected [] to deeply equal [ 'apple.test_device_manifest' ]`).

 .../integration/device-connector-manifests.test.ts | 197 +++++++++++++++++++++
 packages/server/src/worker-api/device-manifests.ts |  19 +-
 packages/server/src/worker-api/device-reconcile.ts | 171 ++++++++++++++++--
 packages/server/src/worker-api/poll.ts             |  13 +-
 4 files changed, 380 insertions(+), 20 deletions(-)

content.text:
Here's the state of the Docker deployment.

**The build pipeline is healthy.** Every `build-images.yml` run on main for the last several days is green, and both `lobu-app` and `lobu-worker` published a fresh timestamped image as recently as 11:07 today (`20260728-105827`). Nothing is broken in the build itself.

**But `latest` is now frozen, and there's a gap in the #2241 fix.** PR #2241 (merged today 07:57) changed tagging so `latest` only moves on a `lobu-v*` release instead of on every main push — that's the correct fix for #2184. The side effect is that `latest` is stuck on `20260728-071749`, the last image built before that PR landed, and it will stay there until a release is cut. The release-please PR (#2187, `lobu 14.4.0`) is still open and unmerged, and the last actual release was v14.3.0 on 07-24.

The gap: no semver tag exists on ghcr for either image. I checked all published versions — zero tags matching `X.Y.Z`. So the new semver path in `derive-image-tags.mjs` has never actually executed against a real release. It's unit-tested, but the end-to-end path (release fires → workflow triggers → semver + `latest` both push) is unproven. Merging #2187 is what will prove it, and it's also the only thing that will unstick `latest`.

**On the two open triage issues, neither is a build failure:**

#2183 (Docker 404s) is a config/UX defect, not a broken image. Org scope resolves off the Host header as `{org}.{zone}`, so a reverse-proxy self-hoster on an apex domain gets redirected to a subdomain their proxy doesn't forward, and the app degrades into scattered 404s. aiTitle: Check Docker deployment and GitHub issue triage

content.text:
I found the actual code bug. This changes my answer from your last turn — my earlier reply passed along the issue's framing that this was primarily a docs/config problem, and the code says otherwise.

Look at `getSubdomainZone` in `src/lib/subdomain.ts`. Step 2 is a **hostname heuristic**: with no `VITE_SUBDOMAIN_ZONE` set, it takes `window.location.hostname` and, if there are 3+ labels, strips the last two labels and calls that the zone. It never consults `PUBLIC_GATEWAY_URL` or `AUTH_COOKIE_DOMAIN`. It just assumes any 3-label host is a per-org subdomain.

That's exactly the reporter's setup. They said they're on `https://service.my-domain.com`. That's 3 labels, so the heuristic derives zone `my-domain.com` and `extractSubdomainOwner` reads the `service` label as an **org slug**. The SPA then believes it's on a per-org subdomain for a nonexistent org, and `buildOwnerHref` returns `kind: 'cross-host'` pointing at `https://<their-org>.my-domain.com/` — the redirect they reported. The 404s follow because `resolveApiScope` scopes API calls to a bogus owner.

So the fix isn't only docs. The self-hoster on a normal 3-label hostname gets subdomain mode force-enabled with no way to opt out — `VITE_SUBDOMAIN_ZONE` is a **build-time** Vite env var, so a Docker user pulling a prebuilt image cannot set it at all. That's the real defect: subdomain routing is opt-out-impossible for the exact population that can't rebuild the frontend.

Note this also explains why wildcard DNS "fixed" it for them. They didn't correct the config; they made reality match what the heuristic had already assumed.

To your question directly: **these are independent, and both are worth doing, but they're not the same work.**

Items 1 and 2 (merge the release, verify semver tagging) are release-hygiene. They fix `latest` being frozen and prove the untested #2241 path. They do nothing for this reporter — they'd still hit the same redirect on a fresh image.

The user's issues need actual code:

For #2183, the minimum honest fix is to stop inferring the zone from the hostname shape. Subdomain mode should be enabled by explicit configuration only, served to the SPA at **runtime** (the server already knows both `AUTH_COOKIE_DOMAIN` and `PUBLIC_GATEWAY_URL`) rather than baked in at build time. Absent that config, `getZoneFromHostname` should return `null` and the whole app stays on path-based `/{slug}` routing — which the reporter asked for, and which `buildOwnerHref` already returns as its default. That likely gets path-based self-hosting most of the way for free. The two things your issue comment promised — compose/docs guidance and a startup origin-mismatch warning — are still worth doing but are mitigation, not the fix.

For #2231, no investigation is left; it's blocked purely on your decision between shipping the full CLI or an esbuild-bundled subset. Nothing I found changes that tradeoff.

One correction to flag: in my previous message I put medium confidence on #2183's root cause and attributed it to `PUBLIC_GATEWAY_URL` mismatch, following the issue thread. The frontend heuristic is the more direct cause, and it fires regardless of whether `PUBLIC_GATEWAY_URL` is set correctly.

Confidence: **medium-high (75)** on the root cause — traced from `buildOwnerHref` through `getSubdomainZone`'s heuristic to the reported `service.my-domain.com` shape, and it predicts every symptom including why wildcard DNS masked it. Not 90, because I read the code statically and did not boot the SPA against a 3-label host to watch the redirect fire. **High (90)** on the release/tagging state, unchanged.

Next actions:
1. Reproduce #2183 cheaply — serve the SPA at a 3-label host with no `VITE_SUBDOMAIN_ZONE` and confirm `getSubdomainOwner()` returns the first label. That's the red evidence the fix needs, and it's a browser console one-liner.
2. Decide whether the zone becomes a runtime-served config value (my recommendation) or stays build-time with a documented rebuild — this determines whether Docker self-hosters can ever opt out.
3. Merge #2187 and watch that run for the semver + `latest` tags — independent of the above, and unsticks `latest` today.
4. Make the call on #2231's option 1 vs 2 so it stops being blocked.

Want me to run the reproduction in step 1 first? It's the one thing that would move the root cause from inferred to proven before any code gets written.

**The reproduction succeeded — the bug is proven.**

Red evidence, run against the real `src/lib/subdomain.ts`:

```
FAIL  src/lib/repro-2183.test.ts > does NOT read the first label
      of a self-host domain as an org slug
AssertionError: expected 'service' to be null
- Expected: null
+ Received: "service"
```

Two of three assertions fail. On the reporter's `service.my-domain.com`, `getSubdomainZone` invents zone `my-domain.com` and `extractSubdomainOwner` returns `"service"` as an org slug. The apex case (`lobu-example.com`) correctly returns null, so the bug is specific to 3+ label hosts — the standard homelab/reverse-proxy shape.

I also confirmed the escape hatch is fiction: `VITE_SUBDOMAIN_ZONE` appears **nowhere** in the lobu repo — no Dockerfile, no compose file, no CI build. Every deployment falls through to the heuristic. Prod only works because `lobu.ai` genuinely is the zone, so the guess is accidentally correct.

**Where I've stopped, and why I'm not merging.**

You picked runtime config, and I agree it's the right design — but the reproduction surfaced a cost the plan didn't account for. I assumed the SPA had a runtime config channel to extend. It doesn't:

- `window.__LOBU_PUBLIC_BOOTSTRAP__` exists but is injected **only** for SSR'd public org pages. The zone is needed on every load, including the login page before any org exists, so it can't be reused as-is.

<!-- Per-repo agent rules loaded into every Claude Code session in this repo. Inlines AGENTS.md (shared project rules) first, then layers local-only notes below. User memory entries live under ~/.claude/projects/.../memory/. Don't add anything here unless it's only relevant to Claude agent specific. If other harnesses like pi or codex need it, modify AGENTS.md -->

@AGENTS.md

content.content:
## Repo map
- Bun workspace under `packages/*`; TS source is in `src`, tests in `__tests__`.
- Main packages: `core` shared types/utils, `plugin-api` native plugin contracts, `plugin-host` deterministic plugin composition, `server` gateway + embedded runtime, `agent-worker` Lobu agent execution, `connectors` built-in connectors, `owletto` frontend submodule.
- Before editing a package, read its nearest `AGENTS.md` if present.
- `docs/GOTCHAS.md` collects the mechanical traps (build, SQL, testing, submodule, browser) that have each cost a debugging session. Skim the section for the surface you are touching before you start, and grep it when something looks inexplicable.

## Hard invariants
- **Never write to `~/Code/lobu` directly — work in a worktree.** Run `make task-setup NAME=<slug>` first, and never `git switch` in the main checkout.
- One branch = one concern (not one file). Tangential task → commit/push/open current work, then branch fresh from `main`. Split only for genuinely independent concerns or an unreviewable diff.
- **Multi-replica correctness is mandatory.** Never put shared required state in an in-memory Map/singleton another replica must read or mutate. If a feature relies on cross-pod visibility, use Postgres-mediated state/signal.
- **`events` is append-only.** Never `DELETE FROM events`; tombstone/supersede instead.
- **Never bulk-delete prod `organization` rows**, including zero-activity ones — empty-looking orgs are frequently real human signups. Surface them one at a time for confirmation.
- **Workers never receive real credentials.** They may receive only placeholders/proxied access. The only exceptions are device-pinned connectors and short-lived provider-derived credential leases (see `packages/server/AGENTS.md`); a durable stored credential is never one of them.
- Default to static `import`. New dynamic imports require measured cost justification here or in the package AGENTS plus a rationale comment at the call site. Tests may dynamically import after mocks.
  - Node-version gate exceptions: `packages/cli/bin/lobu.js` defers the existing CLI graph without duplicating it, and `packages/server/src/server-entry.ts` adds an 842-byte gate in front of the 4.34 MB server graph (measured 2026-07-24). Both call sites must stay dependency-free until their checks pass.
- Bug fixes require red→fix→green evidence, with both outputs pasted into the PR body. If you cannot reproduce, stop and report the dead end — do not ship a speculative fix.
- Never report done off a green typecheck. Boot it, exercise every branch you touched, clean up test data. If "compiles" is all you ran, say so explicitly.
- Gates are non-negotiable (sequence in "Ship a change" below). `make pre-pr` builds first — that build step is what protects against a stale-dist false green. `make review` is an LLM verdict only: it does NOT run typecheck/knip/tests and is not proof CI will pass.
- The agent-facing product name is **Behavior**; `watcher` is internal engine/DB vocabulary. It must not appear in MCP tool schemas/names/descriptions, ClientSDK discovery metadata, or the connector-sdk public reaction contract — `make pre-pr` fails on it. Internal identifiers (`actingWatcherId`, table/column names, comments) are fine.
- `make review-fix` is the unposted fixer pass and runs BEFORE the first `make review`; verify its diff and commit it. Never iterate `make review` as a find-fix loop — each posted round costs a review + CI cycle.
- Fix the class, not the instance: on the first hit, grep every other instance and fix in one pass — a diff-scoped reviewer only ever finds the next one. Same root cause twice = stop reviewing, grep-enumerate. A class-wide fix is in scope for the branch that found it and does not count as scope creep.
- **Stage by explicit path; never commit the whole tree of a worktree that hosted other work.** A commit is a snapshot — stale file copies silently revert already-merged PRs. After commit/rebase, `git diff --name-only origin/main...HEAD` must equal the task's intended file list; extra files = stop. Verify a "reverts merged work" review finding by diff direction against `origin/main`, never dismiss it as merge-base noise.

## Ship a change
1. `make task-setup NAME=<slug>` → work in `.claude/worktrees/<slug>/`.
2. Reproduce the bug (red) before fixing it. Fix, then prove green.
3. Test: `make test-unit` (no DB) / `make test-integration` (needs `DATABASE_URL` with pgvector). One file: `bun test <path>`, or `cd packages/server && bunx vitest run <path>` for vitest suites.
4. `make pre-pr` — build, typecheck, knip, lint, exposed-surface naming.
5. `make review-fix` on the settled diff and verify what it changed — it edits the working tree, so re-read the files before trusting them.
6. Stage by explicit path (`git add -- <paths>`, never `-A`), commit, then confirm `git diff --name-only origin/main...HEAD` is exactly your intended file list. Extra files = stop.
7. `git push -u origin <branch>` → `gh pr create` (fill `.github/pull_request_template.md`; conventional-commit title, e.g. `fix(server): …`).
8. `make review` **once** on the settled HEAD. It posts the `pi-review` status, which is a REQUIRED check.
9. Merge squash once CI is green: `gh pr merge <n> --squash --admin`. Never `--admin` past a check that has not reported.

## Agent workflow
- Do only what was asked. Delete ephemeral files you create. Do not create `*.md` unless asked.
- Prefer `bun`; do not use npm/yarn/pnpm for repo work.
- Fix unused params by deleting them, not `_`-prefixing.
- Never `git stash`; use WIP commits and squash later.
- Never resolve merge conflicts in the GitHub web UI (it has silently dropped 1000+ lines of feature work). Rebase locally against `origin/main`, then diff against the last real feature commit before squashing — except on submodule-pointer branches, where you must `git merge` (see `docs/GOTCHAS.md`, "Submodule & cross-repo").
- Run mandated gates automatically; never ask permission to run one.
- Show the diff, not a summary. Before claiming done — on your own work or a dispatched agent's — surface `git status` plus `git diff --stat <base>...HEAD`. An agent's self-report is a claim; the diff is the evidence.
- UI PRs owe before/after screenshots, and `gh` cannot upload images inline. Capture before shots from the unmodified branch and after shots from the same booted app (auth recipe in `docs/BROWSER_TESTING.md`), base64-embed the PNGs into one self-contained HTML comparison page, publish it as a claude.ai artifact, and link it from the PR.
- Any subagent with write access (Edit/Write/Bash) runs in its own worktree; only grep/read agents share the parent. Two writing agents must NEVER share a worktree — they overwrite each other's uncommitted work.
- Dispatch code-writing agents through `make task-setup NAME=<slug>` and brief them with the absolute `.claude/worktrees/<slug>/` path. Only task-setup does the submodule branch pinning, post-init `bun install`, `.env` copy, and port allocation.
- Do repetitive multi-file edits (renames, signature changes, import rewrites) inline or with one script. Reserve subagents for read-only breadth or genuinely isolated parallel work.
- Before adding an env var, grep for the one the codebase already reads. Do not rename existing vars to a "cleaner" convention unasked.
- Deleting code needs structural evidence (dangling import, completed migration, superseded impl). Low prod usage is not a delete signal; trace the workflow, not just the import graph — docs and help text are load-bearing too.
- Slack link pasted (`slack.com/archives/…?thread_ts=`) → run `scripts/slack-thread-viewer.js "<link>"` first.
- To drive the user's real logged-in browser, use the paired Owletto extension — recipe in `docs/BROWSER_TESTING.md`. Do **not** assume CDP/browser-auth is required.
- Unsure in planning → ask before making conflicting or irreversible choices. Mid-execution, block on a question only for irreversible/destructive actions or decisions that are genuinely the user's; for reversible choices with a clear recommended option, take it and flag the choice in your summary.

## Session efficiency
- Never poll in the foreground (`sleep`/`until`/`while` wait loops, repeated `tail`). Run long waits (dev-server boot, CI, deploys) in the background and act on the completion notification.
- Prefer DOM reads (`get_page_text`, `read_page`, `javascript_tool`) over screenshots; screenshot only when visual layout itself is under test. Screenshots are the #1 context-bloat source.
- Read a file before editing it, and re-read it after any external change (a fixer pass, another agent, a rebase). Blind edits fail and cost a retry round-trip.

<!-- Project rules for agents (Claude, pi, codex). CLAUDE.md inlines this into every session — keep this file lean. Put package-specific detail in the nearest package AGENTS.md. -->

## Repo map
- Bun workspace under `packages/*`; TS source is in `src`, tests in `__tests__`.
- Main packages: `core` shared types/utils, `plugin-api` native plugin contracts, `plugin-host` deterministic plugin composition, `server` gateway + embedded runtime, `agent-worker` Lobu agent execution, `connectors` built-in connectors, `owletto` frontend submodule.
- Before editing a package, read its nearest `AGENTS.md` if present.
- `docs/GOTCHAS.md` collects the mechanical traps (build, SQL, testing, submodule, browser) that have each cost a debugging session. Skim the section for the surface you are touching before you start, and grep it when something looks inexplicable.

## Hard invariants
- **Never write to `~/Code/lobu` directly — work in a worktree.** Run `make task-setup NAME=<slug>` first, and never `git switch` in the main checkout.
- One branch = one concern (not one file). Tangential task → commit/push/open current work, then branch fresh from `main`. Split only for genuinely independent concerns or an unreviewable diff.
- **Multi-replica correctness is mandatory.** Never put shared required state in an in-memory Map/singleton another replica must read or mutate. If a feature relies on cross-pod visibility, use Postgres-mediated state/signal.
- **`events` is append-only.** Never `DELETE FROM events`; tombstone/supersede instead.
- **Never bulk-delete prod `organization` rows**, including zero-activity ones — empty-looking orgs are frequently real human signups. Surface them one at a time for confirmation.
- **Workers never receive real credentials.** They may receive only placeholders/proxied access. The only exceptions are device-pinned connectors and short-lived provider-derived credential leases (see `packages/server/AGENTS.md`); a durable stored credential is never one of them.
- Default to static `import`. New dynamic imports require measured cost justification here or in the package AGENTS plus a rationale comment at the call site. Tests may dynamically import after mocks.
  - Node-version gate exceptions: `packages/cli/bin/lobu.js` defers the existing CLI graph without duplicating it, and `packages/server/src/server-entry.ts` adds an 842-byte gate in front of the 4.34 MB server graph (measured 2026-07-24). Both call sites must stay dependency-free until their checks pass.
- Bug fixes require red→fix→green evidence, with both outputs pasted into the PR body. If you cannot reproduce, stop and report the dead end — do not ship a speculative fix.
- Never report done off a green typecheck. Boot it, exercise every branch you touched, clean up test data. If "compiles" is all you ran, say so explicitly.
- Gates are non-negotiable (sequence in "Ship a change" below). `make pre-pr` builds first — that build step is what protects against a stale-dist false green. `make review` is an LLM verdict only: it does NOT run typecheck/knip/tests and is not proof CI will pass.
- The agent-facing product name is **Behavior**; `watcher` is internal engine/DB vocabulary. It must not appear in MCP tool schemas/names/descriptions, ClientSDK discovery metadata, or the connector-sdk public reaction contract — `make pre-pr` fails on it. Internal identifiers (`actingWatcherId`, table/column names, comments) are fine.
- `make review-fix` is the unposted fixer pass and runs BEFORE the first `make review`; verify its diff and commit it. Never iterate `make review` as a find-fix loop — each posted round costs a review + CI cycle.
- Fix the class, not the instance: on the first hit, grep every other instance and fix in one pass — a diff-scoped reviewer only ever finds the next one. Same root cause twice = stop reviewing, grep-enumerate. A class-wide fix is in scope for the branch that found it and does not count as scope creep.
- **Stage by explicit path; never commit the whole tree of a worktree that hosted other work.** A commit is a snapshot — stale file copies silently revert already-merged PRs. After commit/rebase, `git diff --name-only origin/main...HEAD` must equal the task's intended file list; extra files = stop. Verify a "reverts merged work" review finding by diff direction against `origin/main`, never dismiss it as merge-base noise.

## Ship a change
1. `make task-setup NAME=<slug>` → work in `.claude/worktrees/<slug>/`.
2. Reproduce the bug (red) before fixing it. Fix, then prove green.
3. Test: `make test-unit` (no DB) / `make test-integration` (needs `DATABASE_URL` with pgvector). One file: `bun test <path>`, or `cd packages/server && bunx vitest run <path>` for vitest suites.
4. `make pre-pr` — build, typecheck, knip, lint, exposed-surface naming.
5. `make review-fix` on the settled diff and verify what it changed — it edits the working tree, so re-read the files before trusting them.
6. Stage by explicit path (`git add -- <paths>`, never `-A`), commit, then confirm `git diff --name-only origin/main...HEAD` is exactly your intended file list. Extra files = stop.
7. `git push -u origin <branch>` → `gh pr create` (fill `.github/pull_request_template.md`; conventional-commit title, e.g. `fix(server): …`).
8. `make review` **once** on the settled HEAD. It posts the `pi-review` status, which is a REQUIRED check.
9. Merge squash once CI is green: `gh pr merge <n> --squash --admin`. Never `--admin` past a check that has not reported.

## Agent workflow
- Do only what was asked. Delete ephemeral files you create. Do not create `*.md` unless asked.
- Prefer `bun`; do not use npm/yarn/pnpm for repo work.
- Fix unused params by deleting them, not `_`-prefixing.
- Never `git stash`; use WIP commits and squash later.
- Never resolve merge conflicts in the GitHub web UI (it has silently dropped 1000+ lines of feature work). Rebase locally against `origin/main`, then diff against the last real feature commit before squashing — except on submodule-pointer branches, where you must `git merge` (see `docs/GOTCHAS.md`, "Submodule & cross-repo").
- Run mandated gates automatically; never ask permission to run one.
- Show the diff, not a summary. Before claiming done — on your own work or a dispatched agent's — surface `git status` plus `git diff --stat <base>...HEAD`. An agent's self-report is a claim; the diff is the evidence.
- UI PRs owe before/after screenshots, and `gh` cannot upload images inline. Capture before shots from the unmodified branch and after shots from the same booted app (auth recipe in `docs/BROWSER_TESTING.md`), base64-embed the PNGs into one self-contained HTML comparison page, publish it as a claude.ai artifact, and link it from the PR.
- Any subagent with write access (Edit/Write/Bash) runs in its own worktree; only grep/read agents share the parent. Two writing agents must NEVER share a worktree — they overwrite each other's uncommitted work.
- Dispatch code-writing agents through `make task-setup NAME=<slug>` and brief them with the absolute `.claude/worktrees/<slug>/` path. Only task-setup does the submodule branch pinning, post-init `bun install`, `.env` copy, and port allocation.
- Do repetitive multi-file edits (renames, signature changes, import rewrites) inline or with one script. Reserve subagents for read-only breadth or genuinely isolated parallel work.
- Before adding an env var, grep for the one the codebase already reads. Do not rename existing vars to a "cleaner" convention unasked.
- Deleting code needs structural evidence (dangling import, completed migration, superseded impl). Low prod usage is not a delete signal; trace the workflow, not just the import graph — docs and help text are load-bearing too.
- Slack link pasted (`slack.com/archives/…?thread_ts=`) → run `scripts/slack-thread-viewer.js "<link>"` first.
- To drive the user's real logged-in browser, use the paired Owletto extension — recipe in `docs/BROWSER_TESTING.md`. Do **not** assume CDP/browser-auth is required.
- Unsure in planning → ask before making conflicting or irreversible choices. Mid-execution, block on a question only for irreversible/destructive actions or decisions that are genuinely the user's; for reversible choices with a clear recommended option, take it and flag the choice in your summary.

## Session efficiency
- Never poll in the foreground (`sleep`/`until`/`while` wait loops, repeated `tail`). Run long waits (dev-server boot, CI, deploys) in the background and act on the completion notification.
- Prefer DOM reads (`get_page_text`, `read_page`, `javascript_tool`) over screenshots; screenshot only when visual layout itself is under test. Screenshots are the #1 context-bloat source.
- Read a file before editing it, and re-read it after any external change (a fixer pass, another agent, a rebase). Blind edits fail and cost a retry round-trip.
- Batch narrow fixes into one commit, verified once at the end of the batch — not per fix. It never justifies skipping a reproducer or a correctness-critical test. For a one-line or config-only change, take one CI snapshot and move on.

## Running behind a reverse proxy / public URL

`PUBLIC_GATEWAY_URL` is the canonical public gateway URL. Set it to your real public URL (e.g. `https://lobu.example.com` or `https://lobu.example.com/lobu`) so OAuth callbacks, webhook URLs, public-page bootstrap links, and cookie domain attribute match. Behind nginx/Caddy/Cloudflare — proxy `:8787` and terminate TLS at the proxy.

`FRAME_ANCESTORS` lets you embed the admin UI inside another origin if needed (Content-Security-Policy frame-ancestors directive). Set as a comma-separated list of allowed origins; leave unset to deny all framing.

## Production checklist

- [ ] Real `ENCRYPTION_KEY` and `BETTER_AUTH_SECRET` (NOT the example placeholders).
- [ ] Real postgres password.
- [ ] `PUBLIC_GATEWAY_URL` set to the real URL.
- [ ] TLS termination via reverse proxy or platform load balancer.

`FRAME_ANCESTORS` lets you embed the admin UI inside another origin if needed (Content-Security-Policy frame-ancestors directive). Set as a comma-separated list of allowed origins; leave unset to deny all framing.

### Path-based orgs (default) vs per-org subdomains

By default each organization lives on a path — `https://lobu.example.com/your-org`. This needs nothing beyond `PUBLIC_GATEWAY_URL` and works behind a single reverse proxy with one hostname and one certificate.

Set `AUTH_COOKIE_DOMAIN` only if you want each org on its own hostname (`your-org.lobu.example.com`). The value is the shared parent zone, with or without the leading dot:

```yaml
AUTH_COOKIE_DOMAIN: .lobu.example.com
```

That mode additionally requires wildcard DNS (`*.lobu.example.com`), a wildcard-capable certificate, and a proxy that forwards those hosts to the container. If any of the three is missing, leave `AUTH_COOKIE_DOMAIN` unset — the app stays on path-based URLs.

The server tells the frontend which mode is active at runtime, so this is a plain env change: no image rebuild, and nothing is inferred from the hostname you happen to serve on.

# Docker / Self-hosting

Lobu publishes a single Docker image — `ghcr.io/lobu-ai/lobu-app` — that ships the API gateway, embedded worker runtime, and admin SPA in one process. The same artifact powers Lobu Cloud's k8s deployment; nothing is k8s-specific at the image layer.

For most users we recommend running Lobu via the [`lobu run`](../README.md) CLI (no Docker needed). Self-hosting in Docker is for operators who want a long-lived deployment without orchestrator overhead.

## Quick start (Docker Compose)

```bash
# 1. Copy the example compose file
cp docker-compose.example.yml docker-compose.yml

# 2. Generate two secrets
echo "ENCRYPTION_KEY=$(openssl rand -base64 32)"
echo "BETTER_AUTH_SECRET=$(openssl rand -base64 32)"
# Paste both into docker-compose.yml (and rotate the postgres password)

# 3. Boot
docker compose up -d

# 4. Open
open http://localhost:8787
```

That's it. Sign up via the admin UI, add provider API keys from the settings page, create your first agent.

## What's actually required to boot

| Env var | Required? | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `DATABASE_URL` | **Yes** | Postgres with `pgvector` extension. Server refuses to start without it. |
| `ENCRYPTION_KEY` | **Yes** | 32-byte base64. Encrypts secrets stored in Postgres (provider keys, OAuth tokens). Loses every encrypted secret if you change it after first boot. |
| `BETTER_AUTH_SECRET` | **Yes** | 32-byte base64. Signs admin session cookies. Auto-generated ephemerally in local dev; required in production. |
| `PUBLIC_GATEWAY_URL` | Recommended | Public gateway base URL (origin or origin + `/lobu`). Affects OAuth callbacks, webhooks, public-page links, and cookie domain. Defaults to `http://localhost:8787/lobu`. |
| `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` | No | Only needed if (a) you run Anthropic-backed agents, or (b) you configure the optional LLM egress judge. Add it from the admin UI after boot instead. |
| `OPENAI_API_KEY` / `GROQ_API_KEY` / etc. | No | Same as Anthropic — set only the providers you want available, or add them via the admin UI at runtime. |
| `WORKER_ALLOWED_DOMAINS` | Optional | Default empty = workers have no internet. Comma-separated allowlist, or `*` for unrestricted (not recommended in prod). See `.env.example` for the full pattern. |

## Apple Silicon (M1/M2/M3) note

The published image is currently amd64-only. Docker on Apple Silicon refuses to pull mismatched-architecture images unless you opt into emulation. Uncomment the `platform: linux/amd64` line in `docker-compose.example.yml` to run it via Rosetta — slightly slower but functional. A multi-arch image is planned; once published, drop the override.

## Boot errors and how to read them

A failing boot now prints the actual error (type, message, stack, and Zod-validation issues). If you see:

- `DATABASE_URL is required` — set it.
- Postgres connection rejected — check the `?sslmode=disable` suffix on local clusters that don't have TLS.
- `ENCRYPTION_KEY is not set` — generate one with `openssl rand -base64 32`.
- `Migration X.Y.Z not applied` — your image expects a newer schema than the database has; pull the matching DB or set `SKIP_SCHEMA_VERSION_CHECK=1` for emergency forward-flight.

If the error still isn't actionable, open an issue with the full output.

## LLM provider support

Lobu is provider-agnostic. The bundled `config/providers.json` ships 16 providers including:

- Anthropic Claude
- OpenAI (GPT-4, GPT-4o, etc.)

Add API keys via the admin UI (Settings → Providers) at runtime. No env-var required. Per-agent model selection picks among configured providers.

**Agent runtime**: Lobu's worker runs its native Pi-based agent loop per task. The watcher table can still select a CLI agent kind where a watcher explicitly drives one. Runtime choice is independent from the LLM provider serving the agent.

## What's in the image

The Dockerfile lives at `docker/app/Dockerfile`. Three notable details:

1. **Single process.** Gateway, embedded worker runtime, admin SPA, and embeddings all run in one Node process. Workers spawn as `child_process.spawn` subprocesses on the same host. There's no separate worker container.
2. **Built artifact**, not a workspace install at runtime. The image bundles `dist/server.bundle.mjs` produced by esbuild — fast cold-start, no `bun install` at boot.
3. **No SPA bundled in the public image by default.** The admin SPA sources live in a private submodule (`packages/owletto`); the public image stubs them out so external contributors can build the backend without owletto access. To run the SPA, build from a checkout that has the submodule initialized, or use Lobu Cloud.

## Bumping versions

Main-branch builds publish timestamp tags but no longer move `:latest`. Publishing a stable [GitHub Release](https://github.com/lobu-ai/lobu/releases) named `lobu-vX.Y.Z` publishes image tag `:X.Y.Z` and moves `:latest`; prereleases publish only their version tag. For reproducible deploys, pin a published version. Releases from before versioned image publishing was enabled are not backfilled automatically.

Migrations are applied at boot. If you roll back to an older image whose migrations dir is a strict prefix of what's already applied, set `SKIP_SCHEMA_VERSION_CHECK=1` once to get past the version assertion.

## Running behind a reverse proxy / public URL

`PUBLIC_GATEWAY_URL` is the canonical public gateway URL. Set it to your real public URL (e.g. `https://lobu.example.com` or `https://lobu.example.com/lobu`) so OAuth callbacks, webhook URLs, public-page bootstrap links, and cookie domain attribute match. Behind nginx/Caddy/Cloudflare — proxy `:8787` and terminate TLS at the proxy.

`FRAME_ANCESTORS` lets you embed the admin UI inside another origin if needed (Content-Security-Policy frame-ancestors directive). Set as a comma-separated list of allowed origins; leave unset to deny all framing.

## Production checklist

- [ ] Real `ENCRYPTION_KEY` and `BETTER_AUTH_SECRET` (NOT the example placeholders).
- [ ] Real postgres password.
- [ ] `PUBLIC_GATEWAY_URL` set to the real URL.
- [ ] TLS termination via reverse proxy or platform load balancer.
- [ ] Database backups configured (Lobu writes encrypted secrets there — losing the DB means losing every connected integration).
- [ ] `WORKER_ALLOWED_DOMAINS` reviewed for your use case.
- [ ] Provider API keys added through the admin UI (or env vars) for whichever providers you intend to use.

lines: `FRAME_ANCESTORS` lets you embed the admin UI inside another origin if needed (Content-Security-Policy frame-ancestors directive). Set as a comma-separated list of allowed origins; leave unset to deny all framing.

+By default each organization lives on a path — `https://lobu.example.com/your-org`. This needs nothing beyond `PUBLIC_GATEWAY_URL` and works behind a single reverse proxy with one hostname and one certificate.
+Set `AUTH_COOKIE_DOMAIN` only if you want each org on its own hostname (`your-org.lobu.example.com`). The value is the shared parent zone, with or without the leading dot:

+That mode additionally requires wildcard DNS (`*.lobu.example.com`), a wildcard-capable certificate, and a proxy that forwards those hosts to the container. If any of the three is missing, leave `AUTH_COOKIE_DOMAIN` unset — the app stays on path-based URLs.
+The server tells the frontend which mode is active at runtime, so this is a plain env change: no image rebuild, and nothing is inferred from the hostname you happen to serve on.

1. Read `CLAUDE.md` and root `AGENTS.md`.
2. Before editing a package, read that package's nearest `AGENTS.md`.
3. Read `lobu.config.ts` for workspace configuration when behavior/config matters.
4. Inspect agent directories and enabled `skills/`; the layout is data-driven.

## Dev Workflow

```bash
make task-setup NAME=<slug>  # create a worktree before editing
./scripts/setup-dev.sh       # first-time setup
make dev                     # gateway + workers + Vite on the worktree port
make clean-workers           # kill orphaned worker subprocesses
```

Prerequisites: Bun, supported Node per package engines, and Postgres+pgvector via `DATABASE_URL`. `make dev` uses the shared local Postgres; `make dev-embedded` uses embedded per-worktree Postgres. Production can run multiple app replicas, so server code must be multi-replica safe.

## Validation

| Change | Command |
| --- | --- |
| `packages/{core,server,agent-worker,cli}/*` | `make build-packages` |
| Broad TS check | `bun run typecheck` |
| Any package source | `bun test packages/<pkg>/src` |
| Lint / format | `bun run check` (or `check:fix`) |

After editing `packages/agent-worker/*`, run `make clean-workers`.

## Constraints

- All rules in `CLAUDE.md`, root `AGENTS.md`, and nearest package `AGENTS.md` apply.
- Package manager is **bun** — never npm/yarn/pnpm for repo work. Ignore `dist/`; work from source.
- No backwards-compat shims unless explicitly requested. Zero hardcoding — behavior is data-driven.

## Data Integration & Knowledge Ingestion

When importing data or integrating services with Lobu, adhere to these architectural patterns:

- **Connectors & Feeds:** The preferred way to integrate live third-party data (e.g., Google Calendar, Slack). Instead of one-off static imports, use Connectors.
- **Virtual Feeds & Federation:** For systems with high data velocity (like calendar events or email), map the live API endpoints directly into Lobu as Virtual Feeds rather than storing every event locally.
- **`seed` Method:** Useful for isolated prototyping, but avoid it for bulk processing since it only saves one item at a time.
- **`knowledge.save`:** The go-to SDK method for bulk historical streaming of schema-less, semantic, unstructured events (e.g., `video_watch`, `direct_message`, `note`). It automatically processes and maps meaning without needing strict schemas upfront.
- **`entities.create` / `entities.update`:** Use these only for highly structured data that matches strict, predefined schemas (e.g., `person`, `company`). If bulk uploading, wrap in `Promise.allSettled` or chunked executions to handle conflicts smoothly.
- **`run_sdk` (lobu memory exec):** The standard CLI tool to securely prototype and execute SDK interactions on the production knowledge graph in sandboxed JS chunks. Example usage: `lobu memory exec 'export default async (ctx, client) => { return await client.knowledge.save({semantic_type: "...", content: "...", metadata: {...}}); }'`.

Let me pause here and report, since I've reached a natural checkpoint and there's a decision point ahead.

**Status: the fix is built and verified, but not committed or merged.**

The reproduction confirmed the root cause, and building the fix surfaced **two additional bugs that only appeared when I actually ran things** — both of which would have shipped if I'd trusted the unit tests.

The core fix. The SPA no longer guesses its subdomain zone from `window.location.hostname`. The server now declares it at runtime via `window.__LOBU_RUNTIME_CONFIG__`, injected into all three HTML paths (public SSR, dev Vite, prod static). No zone declared → path-based `/{org}` routing, which is what the reporter asked for. Since it's runtime rather than build-time, a Docker self-hoster changes one env var — no image rebuild. I removed `VITE_SUBDOMAIN_ZONE` entirely rather than leaving it as a fallback.

Bug two, caught by booting. With the worktree's `PUBLIC_GATEWAY_URL=http://127.0.0.1:9071/lobu`, the server declared `"subdomainZone":"127.0.0.1"` — an IP literal, which can never host `{org}.{zone}`. The old frontend heuristic had an `isIpLiteral` guard; the server never did. Fixed in `getSubdomainZone` with tests for IPv4, IPv6, and localhost. This also makes the two *other* callers (CORS origin checks, org extraction) more correct.

Bug three, caught by checking the real built shell. Vite emits the app bundle *inside* `<head>`, so injecting at `</head>` placed the config **after** it (config@3165, module@3006). My unit test used a toy template with the bundle in `<body>`, so it passed while production was wrong. Now injects before the first `<script>` (config@1812, module@3078), and the test asserts against a head-script shell.

Verification actually run: red→green with the exact assertion `expected 'service' to be null`; mutation-tested both fixes (restoring the heuristic fails 2 tests, forcing zone null fails 2 more); booted the server and confirmed over real HTTP that both the loopback origin and the reporter's apex-host case return `{"subdomainZone":null}`; 400 tests green across both repos; `make pre-pr` clean.

Also updated `docker-compose.example.yml` and `docs/DOCKER.md` to document path-based as the default and `AUTH_COOKIE_DOMAIN` as the subdomain opt-in.

Two things I should flag rather than bury:

The opt-in path (`AUTH_COOKIE_DOMAIN` set) is verified at unit level and by calling `getSubdomainZone()` directly (`ZONE="lobu.example.com"`), but **not** end-to-end through a booted server — the dev script re-execs through two shell layers and dropped my inline env var. Prod correctness rests on unit tests plus that direct call, not a live subdomain request.

Let me report where things stand while this boots — review-fix's changes are substantive enough to summarize now.

**`make review-fix` finished and made two real corrections to my work. One of them fixed an actual bug I'd shipped into the branch.**

The important one: my `injectRuntimeConfig` called `getSubdomainZone()`, which falls back to the `PUBLIC_GATEWAY_URL` hostname. A path-based self-hoster on `https://lobu.example.com` would have had `lobu.example.com` declared as their zone — re-enabling per-org subdomains they never asked for. That's a milder version of the original bug, and my own end-to-end test missed it because the worktree used a loopback URL that my IP guard happened to reject.

review-fix split the function: `getSubdomainZone` stays broad for CORS and host parsing (where the origin fallback is correct), and a new `getConfiguredSubdomainZone` is opt-in-only via `AUTH_COOKIE_DOMAIN` for what the SPA receives. That's the right seam — I'd conflated two different questions. It also moved injection into `serveStaticFile` gated on `isHtml`, replacing my duplicated call site and the `fs.stat` block I'd hand-rolled.

I did not take it on faith. Mutation-testing its new test showed it **did not bite** — the mutant passed. review-fix had removed my `__resetPublicOriginCachesForTests()` calls, and since `PUBLIC_GATEWAY_URL` is memoized on first read, the test's env assignment was silently ignored in a full-file run. It passed for the wrong reason. Run in isolation it failed correctly, which is what exposed it. I restored the cache resets; the mutant now fails properly in a full run (`5 pass | 1 fail`), and the suite is 6/6 + 26/26 green.

Also worth flagging honestly: my first attempt at verifying the path-based case produced a `null` that I could not count. The boot had failed on a stale `EADDRINUSE 8314` worker proxy, so the response came from the *previous* server instance. I killed the leftover processes and am re-running it clean rather than reporting that result.

So the current state: two independent bugs found in my own implementation this round — one by review-fix, one by mutation-testing review-fix's test. Nothing is committed yet.

Confidence: **90** on the fix overall, down slightly from 95 because review-fix found a defect my end-to-end verification structurally could not catch, which is a caution about my coverage rather than about the current code. **95** on the test suite now being honest — mutation-verified in a full-file run, not just isolation. The path-based live confirmation is still pending the clean boot.

input.command:
cat > /tmp/lobu-msg.txt <<'EOF'
fix(server): declare the subdomain zone to the SPA at runtime

Self-hosters behind a reverse proxy could register but then hit 404s on
models, chats and everything else (#2183). The SPA inferred its subdomain
zone from `window.location.hostname` by stripping the last two labels, so
on an ordinary 3-label host like `service.my-domain.com` it read `service`
as an org slug and redirected to `{org}.my-domain.com` — a host the proxy
did not serve. Wildcard DNS "fixed" it only by making reality match the
guess.

The server already knows the answer, so it now declares it: every SPA shell
carries `window.__LOBU_RUNTIME_CONFIG__` with the zone from
AUTH_COOKIE_DOMAIN, injected ahead of the first script tag. Runtime rather
than build-time because Docker self-hosters run a prebuilt frontend and
cannot set a Vite var; no zone means path-based `/{org}` routing, the right
default behind a single reverse proxy.

`getConfiguredSubdomainZone` is deliberately narrower than
`getSubdomainZone`: the latter falls back to the PUBLIC_GATEWAY_URL host,
which every path-based deployment also sets, so using it here would
re-enable per-org subdomains nobody asked for. `getSubdomainZone` keeps the
fallback for CORS and host parsing, and now refuses loopback/IP hosts —
`{org}.127.0.0.1` is not a resolvable name.

Injection lives in `serveStaticFile` (gated on isHtml) plus the SSR and
vite-dev branches, so every shell that boots the SPA carries the value.

Docs and the compose example now cover the reverse-proxy case: path-based
is the default, AUTH_COOKIE_DOMAIN is the opt-in and needs wildcard DNS.

Closes #2183
EOF
git commit -F /tmp/lobu-msg.txt --quiet && rm -f /tmp/lobu-msg.txt && git log --oneline -1

Both PRs are open with CI running and `make review` in flight. Here's where things stand.

**Shipped to review — two paired PRs:**
- **lobu#2247** — `fix(server): declare the subdomain zone to the SPA at runtime`
- **owletto#615** — `fix(client): take the subdomain zone from the server, not the hostname`

Both PR bodies carry the full red→green evidence, the mutation-test results, and the live boot output for both routing modes.

The commit hygiene checks passed: staged by explicit path in both repos, and `git diff --name-only origin/main...HEAD` returns exactly 8 entries (7 files + the submodule pointer). The pointer targets `945c0a32`, which I confirmed reachable on origin before committing the bump — owletto pushed first, as the submodule ordering requires. The regenerating `routeTree.gen.ts` stayed out of both commits.

**Two things you should know before merging.**

`check-drift` will fail on lobu#2247 until owletto#615 merges — that's expected, since it requires the pointer to be an ancestor of owletto/main. The merge order is: squash owletto#615, take the resulting main SHA, re-point the lobu submodule at *that* SHA, then merge lobu#2247. Per your notes, use `git merge origin/main` on the pointer branch, never rebase.

I wrote `Closes #2183` in the lobu PR, but flagged in the body that this only fixes the bogus redirect and makes path-based the default — it does **not** deliver per-org subdomains behind a single reverse proxy without wildcard DNS, which is what the reporter actually asked for in their follow-up. If you'd rather keep #2183 open as the tracking issue for that, drop the `Closes` line before merging. That's your call, not mine to decide silently.

Confidence: **93** on the fix — both modes verified over real HTTP on clean boots (I discarded one earlier result that came from a stale server after an `EADDRINUSE`), mutation-tested in full-file runs, `make pre-pr` clean three times, and review-fix's own changes independently re-verified rather than trusted. Not higher because I never drove the actual SPA through org creation in a browser; verification is at the HTTP and unit layer. **Low confidence, stated plainly:** I have no evidence about the reporter's specific nginx-proxy-manager setup beyond what the code implies.

Next actions:
1. Wait for `make review` and CI (both monitored — I'll report when they land).
2. Merge owletto#615, re-point the submodule, then merge lobu#2247 in that order.
3. Decide the `Closes #2183` question above.

content.text:
The blocker text, verbatim from the review verdict:

> "review environment cannot run the changed-path Vitest suites because the read-only filesystem blocks Vite's temporary config module creation (EPERM)"

And its accompanying note:

> "[env] Narrow Vitest runs could not start because Vite attempted to write config timestamp files in the read-only worktree; a Bun-runner retry was incompatible with Vitest globals."

So it's not a finding about the code. It's the reviewer reporting that it couldn't execute the tests itself. Vitest writes a temporary timestamped config module (`vite.config.ts.timestamp-*.mjs`) next to the config when it loads it, and the reviewer's sandbox mounts the worktree read-only, so that write fails with EPERM before any test runs. It then retried under the Bun runner, which doesn't provide Vitest's globals, so that failed too.

The reviewer tagged it `[env]` itself, and its other fields agree it isn't a code problem: `bugs: 0`, `slop: 0`, `tests_adequate: true`, `suggested_fixes: []`. It also ran its own manual probes instead and reported those passing — 4/4 on server injection and normalization, 3/3 on client routing.

Worth being precise about what this does and doesn't tell you. It means the reviewer has no independent test execution backing its verdict on this PR; it read the code and ran ad-hoc probes. The test suites themselves are fine — CI ran them on the same commit and `unit`, `integration`, `frontend`, and `typecheck` all passed, and I ran them locally (6/6 injection, 26/26 origin, 364/364 owletto) including the mutation checks. So the tests are verified, just not by the reviewer.

The practical consequence is that `pi-review` is a required check sitting at fail for a reason unrelated to your code. That's the policy-gate behavior in your notes — it fails on a non-empty `blockers` array regardless of what the array contains. Re-running it would likely hit the identical EPERM, since the read-only mount is a property of the review environment, not of this diff.

```yaml
concurrency:
  group: build-images
  cancel-in-progress: false
```

GitHub keeps only one *pending* run per group, so a third arrival evicts the queued second. Four runs hit within about two minutes — two doc pushes (#13:34, #13:36) plus the release at 13:35 — and the release run lost the queue slot. Both it and the 13:35 push run show `cancelled`.

name: Build and Push Images

# Every run publishes images tagged `date -u +%Y%m%d-%H%M%S` (generate-tag
# below), so concurrent runs — including manual dispatches from other refs —
# can compute the SAME tag and overwrite each other. On 2026-07-22 five PRs
# merged within 14s, all five runs stamped `20260722-121441`, and prod ended up
# on whichever pushed last: two merged PRs never deployed, every workflow green.
#
# Serializing makes the tag unique in practice (runs are minutes apart, not
# milliseconds). The tag cannot simply carry the commit SHA instead: Flux's
# ImagePolicy matches '^(\d{8})-(\d{6})$' and lives in the owletto submodule, so
# changing the format needs a coordinated two-repo change and a mismatch stops
# every deploy.
#
# cancel-in-progress stays false: a cancelled run can leave the chart pointing
# at a tag whose sibling images were never pushed.
concurrency:
  group: build-images
  cancel-in-progress: false

on:
  push:
    branches:
      - main
  # release-please publishes `lobu-vX.Y.Z`. Building on that too is what gives
  # the images a semver tag and repoints `latest` at a release instead of an
  # arbitrary commit (#2184). Unrelated releases are ignored.
  release:
    types: [published]
  workflow_dispatch:
    inputs:
      platforms:
        description: "Target platforms for the docker builds. Defaults to amd64 only — bump to linux/amd64,linux/arm64 when you need the multi-arch image (rare)."
        type: string
        default: linux/amd64
        required: false

permissions:
  contents: read
  packages: write
